sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
The **Pureblood Knights** were once the oath-sworn champions of Mohg, Lord of Blood. Esteemed noble servants defined by their extravagant clothing and elegant swordsmanship. These men, along with their master, swore a pact of blood to each other, to one day establish a new and glorious dynasty. The oldest known member of this entourage is the commander, Sir Ansbach, a scholarly gentleman of noble manners and frightfully deadly swordsmanship. When Mohg became ensnared by Miquella's enchantment, Ansbach sought to challenge the ever-youthful demigod in an attempt to free his master. And while he managed to grievously injure the empyrean, Ansbach was ultimately defeated in the confrontation by having his heart stolen, just like his master.

Ansbach's defeat would mark the beginning of a degradation in the values of the Pureblood Knights. Who, in the belief that it could eventually bring about their desired dynasty, would begin to hunt their fellow man in order to harvest their blood and offer it as sacrifice to slake the thirst of Miquella's cocoon. Steadily gaining infamy as nothing more than depraved, blood-crazed zealots that stalk their own. With most of the newer members inaugurated at this time, the Bloody Fingers, being Pureblood Knights in name only.

sections.markdown: Reduvia** is a dagger in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Dropped by Bloody Finger Nerijus near Murkwater Cave once defeated.
 - Beware that progressing through the game can prevent this invasion from happening, more specifically by defeating all the major Limgrave bosses (Flying Dragon Agheel, Mad Pumpkin Head, Margit, the Fell Omen, Tibia Mariner, and Tree Sentinel).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Its skill, Reduvia Blood Blade, is essentially a version of the Blood Blade skill that costs twice as much FP and deals a little less Stance damage in exchange for not costing any HP to cast and having 50% more base Blood Loss (90 instead of 60).
 - Since this skill hits with both the projectile and the blade, it deals much more damage and inflicts more Blood Loss build-up when used within the dagger's range.
 - Ultimately, Blood Blade will do about 4% more damage at half cost with equivalent Arcane and an Occult affinity, making it the stronger alternative if the user is willing to stomach the self-damage and the relatively lower Blood Loss isn't a problem.
- Not counting the Wakizashi this is the strongest dagger for a hybrid Dexterity/Arcane build and the second strongest dagger for a hybrid Strength/Arcane or pure Arcane build, after the Bloodstained Dagger.
 - However, the Bloodstained's advantage is rather slight, only 8 AP (Attack Power) for the Str/Arc build and a mere 1 AP for the pure Arc build and the Reduvia will consistently have 10 more points of Blood Loss build-up.
- Since this weapon has innate Arcane-scaling its innate Blood Loss will scales with that stat.
- The Bandit starting Origin has enough stats to wield this quite strong weapon without any level ups or stat increases.

sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Rejection** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 1,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Rejection produces a shockwave, knocking back enemies within a 2-meter radius and inflicting heavy Stamina damage to guarding enemies—180 in PvE and 220 in PvP—while also dealing 10 Stance damage.

Charging the spell increases the radius to 4 meters, Stamina damage to 220 in PvE and 275 in PvP, and Stance damage to 14.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 9 FP per cast.
- Costs 24 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 31.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- Rejection has 0 Attack Power and deals no damage.
- Knockback occurs in the direction the caster is facing.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- The player model is just under 2 meters tall, making it a useful reference for measuring the spell's reach.
- Although this incantation deals no damage, it can instantly kill enemies or other players by knocking them off edges.
- This spell easily knocks down most flying or jumping foes and can be used to break the Stance of many enemies.
- The knockback effect applies to Crystalians even while armored, breaking their Stance in 7 hits, or 5 hits if charged.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Rejection is one of the few offensive spells that deal no damage.
- Although this spell is affected by the Godfrey Icon when charged, its 0 damage output makes the 15% damage boost irrelevant.
- Patch 1.07: Increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
 - This increased the Stamina damage against guarding enemies from 150 to 180 when uncharged and from 180 to 220 when charged.
 - Stamina damage against guarding players was instead increased to 220 when uncharged and 275 when charged.

sections.markdown:
Rykard was born the son of Radagon, a champion of the Erdtree, and Queen Rennala, head of both the Carian Royal Family and the Academy of Raya Lucaria. He had two siblings, Radahn and Ranni.

At some point, the first Elden Lord, Godfrey, was robbed of grace and hounded from the Lands Between. Rykard's father, Radagon, left Rennala to become Queen Marika's new consort and the second Elden Lord. Rykard and his siblings were thus raised to demigods by their new stepmother, Marika.

Under the Golden Order, Rykard was a ruthless justiciar who commanded a company of inquisitors. His inquisitors persecuted and mercilessly tortured those considered heretics to the Golden Order, such as the Albinaurics. He spent time in the volcanic Mt. Gelmir, where he discovered the ancient magma hexes of a forgotten serpent-worshiping religion native to the region, which he brought back into practical use as new sorceries. Rykard also travelled to a foreign land where he encountered a dancer by the name of Tanith, who he would eventually take as his consort.

Rykard was also known for the construction of the Iron Virgins, automatons which were capable of both battlefield carnage and abducting victims to transport them to the Volcano Manor.

Rykard's budding blasphemous inclinations led him to assist his sister, Ranni, in orchestrating the Night of Black Knives. On the night of the plot, Ranni rewarded Rykard with a slab of rock engraved with the traces of the Rune of Death, which would allow him to challenge the black beast of Destined Death, should the coming trespass one day transpire.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.markdown:
At some point following the the Night of Black Knives, Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring, and her offspring acquired the Great Runes. The maddening taint of their newfound strength led to the Shattering, a war between Marika's demigod descendants, each seeking to become the new ruler of the Lands Between.

Rykard was indignant, and viewed the Erdtree and the gods demanding that the demigods fight over miserly scraps of power to be debasing. He launched a blasphemous campaign against the Erdtree and the Greater Will. When he turned to heresy, taking by force became the rule, the gods themselves being no different. Rykard's ambitions, though blasphemous, marked him a worthy sovereign, and drew many followers to his cause who admired his heroic aspirations. His rebels were known as the Recusants.

Based in the Volcano Manor on Mt. Gelmir, his forces battled the armies of the Leyndell in what would become the most appalling battle of the Shattering, a wretched, unending war with no glory. Acts of cannibalism became a sickening reality across the battlefields, and some forces from both sides became afflicted with the Frenzied Flame sickness.

sections.heading: Blasphemy
sections.markdown:
At some point during the Shattering, Rykard fed himself, Great Rune and all, to the blasphemous serpent that dwelled inside Mt. Gelmir, an ancient traitor to the Erdtree, merging with the creature. In the final moments before being devoured, he briefly had a vision of the future wherein he witnessed a serpent devouring the world.

Following this, his lofty ambition degraded into gluttonous depravity. He fed on his greatest champions, and in the bowels of the serpent, they became the lord's family. Disturbed by what had become of their master and by the costly battles waged in his name, Rykard's forces abandoned him. Some attempted to put him to rest by searching for a mighty weapon capable of killing their lord. Such a weapon was found in the Serpent-Hunter, an enchanted spear crafted to hunt an immortal serpent in the distant past. However, all attempts made to take his life failed. The spear would come to reside in Rykard's chambers, left by a former Recusant who hoped a worthy champion might one day appear to wield it and spare the once-noble Rykard from further dishonor.

When Rykard gave himself to the elder serpent, the birth of the man-serpents followed, the deformed offspring of a repellent birthing ritual. One such man-serpent, known as Zorayas, would go on to be adopted by Tanith, and learn to assume an illusory human form in which she went by Rya. She was unaware of the origins of her birth, as Tanith concealed the truth of the Volcano Manor from her and insisted she was born of the grace of a king. It is implied that the woman known as Daedicar was one such woman subjected to the ritual, the biological mother of Zorayas and other man-serpents.

At some point before giving himself to the serpent, Rykard offered Tanith the Tonic of Forgetfulness to purge her memories of him. However, she refused, claiming "My Lord, there could be no greater distress than to forget you." Tanith was the only human known to stand with Rykard after he merged with the serpent of blasphemy; as in that moment, she was truly charmed by him. The Crucible Knight bodyguard of Tanith may have also served the Volcano Manor before Rykard was devoured, and as such, would have been the second human known to remain loyal, but this remains unknown. Tanith would continue her lord's legacy by leading a new force of Recusants, recruiting unsuspecting Tarnished after their return to the Lands Between following the end of the Shattering. The worthiest of these Tarnished champions would be granted an audience with Rykard, which ended with them being devoured by the serpentine demigod to increase his power further.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown: Eventually, a Tarnished champion managed to reach Rykard's chambers, and defeated the serpentine demigod to claim his Great Rune. Rykard took notice of this and awoke to confront the Tarnished, then pulled out a massive sword from the serpent's mouth, while boasting that they would join the Serpent King as family. After a hard battle, Rykard was ultimately slain by the Tarnished. Upon his death, he claimed "A serpent never dies", proven true when his initially vanished corpse began to regenerate. After Rykard is slain, Tanith suggested she planned to soon depart, having no reason to remain at Volcano Manor. However, afterwards she secretly journeyed to Rykard's chambers and attempted to eat his tremendous corpse, muttering her hopes that Rykard might live on within her, just as he had the serpent.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.markdown:
The fight consists of two distinct phases, each with its own health bar. Phase 1 must be beaten each time to reach phase 2.

The Serpent-Hunter can be found sticking out of a pile of corpses near the entrance to the arena, and can be obtained without alerting the boss. This weapon makes the fight significantly easier, as it produces blades of light when swung that allow for long-distance attacks.

Defeating this boss will terminate Tanith's questline, regardless of how far one has progressed it. Any Volcano Manor targets not yet unlocked will also be missed.

sections.heading: Phase 1 - God-Devouring Serpent
sections.markdown: The God-Devouring Serpent is slow-moving, surrounded by a pool of magma. The magma makes it difficult to get close without taking damage, however the Serpent-Hunter allows for one to attack from a safer distance. It uses a combination of quick biting attacks and eruptions of magma, as well as a poison attack.

sections.heading: Phase 2 - Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
sections.markdown: After reducing the Serpent's health to 0, a cutscene plays and phase 2 begins. Rykard, armed with a sword, moves around the arena similarly to the Serpent, however his moveset is almost entirely new.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.markdown: Rykard's arena is a spacious cavern, dotted with piles of corpses and tall corpse pillars, which can be broken by Rykard's attacks. The size of the arena is helpful for avoiding Rykard's Rancor and Rancor Rain, as one can run around the room until the attack ends.

sections.markdown:

- As seen in the opening cutscene and his paintings, Rykard appears to have light red hair or, arguably, blond hair, in contrast to his direct siblings.

pages.title: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: is a character in Elden Ring. She is a Shardbearer Boss encountered in the Academy of Raya Lucaria. While this encounter is not required to advance the story, Rennala must be defeated to unlock the ability to respec, Moonlight Altar, and "Age of the Stars" ending.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The young Lunar Princess was an astrologer who gazed at the night sky and chased the stars. In her youth, Rennala and her younger sister, Rellana, encountered moons that one day made them champions. Hers was an enchanting full moon. Later, she bewitched the Academy of Raya Lucaria with her lunar magic, becoming its master. She prohibited study of the primeval current at the academy, exiling its founders, Azur and Lusat. She established the house of Caria as royalty and anointed the enchanted Carian Knights, heroes of the highest honors.

When the sorceries of the Carians were still only the prototypes of the latter sword-phalanx sorceries., Rennala gifted a braid of her hair to Rellana, who disavowed her birthright to join Messmer the Impaler in his Crusade in the Realm of Shadow.

In the age of the Erdtree, a champion known as Radagon led Queen Marika's armies against Liurnia of the Lakes. Rennala and the academy rallied forces to repel the invasion. She led her Glintstones Knights and, despite numbering fewer then twenty, their magic made them a match for even the champions of gold in battle. Two Liurnian Wars were fought, both of which saw no clear victor.

Radagon ended the Second Liurnian War by cleansing himself with Celestial Dew. Repenting his territorial aggressions, he swore his love to Rennala. They married at the Church of Vows, uniting the houses of the Erdtree and the Moon. As a Carian Queen, Rennala bestowed Radagon a Moon greatsword in accordance with a long-standing tradition. They had three children: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni. Rennala led young Ranni by the hand to meet her Dark Moon.

Later, Radagon gifted an amber egg, the Great Rune of the Unborn, to Rennala, and left her side to become the second King Consort of Queen Marika, receiving the title of second Elden Lord. When Radagon left, Rennala's heart left with him.

Realizing their heartbroken queen was no champion at all, the Academy rebelled against the Carian Royal Family and Rennala was locked away in the grand library. Clutching the amber egg left to her by Radagon, she dissociated, devoting herself to the grim art of reincarnation. She would use it on Juvenile Scholars found around her, calling them her "sweetings", continuously rebirthing them in an imperfect process which would leave their memories fading into oblivion. The children born anew by Rennala were all frail and short-lived, imperfect beings, each and all.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown:
Rennala remained in the Grand Library throughout the reign of Lord Radagon and the ensuing Shattering war. She hovered idly in the air, clutching her egg, while her reborn Juvenile Scholars sang a lullaby that shielded her in a golden, moonlike bubble.

If the Great Rune separates from Rennala, a protective mechanism activates, releasing a dense black fog. The disembodied voice of Ranni the Witch warns intruders as an illusory image of Rennala emerges from the darkness to battle the player upon a moonlit sea. This apparition reflects Rennala as she once was, at the height of her power.

If the illusion is defeated, the present Rennala regains her egg and sits quietly in her bassinet at the center of the library, calling softly to her timid sweetings.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: A tall, barefooted woman with an immaculate, pale complexion and lustrous black hair. She is dressed in deep blue and red robes with gold trim and wears a large hat curved like the crescent moon.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
- HP: 3,493 (Phase 1)
- HP: 4,097 (Phase 2)
- Defense: 109
- Stance: 0
- Cannot be parried
- Vulnerable to Critical Attacks after her Stance is broken
- Deals Standard and Magic damage
- This boss summons Juvenile Scholars during Phase 1. She summons Wolves, Troll Knights, Flying Dragons, and Bloodhound Knights during Phase 2.
- Drops: 40,000 runes, Remembrance of the Full Moon Queen, and Great Rune of the Unborn

Throughout both phases, Rennala resists magic but is more vulnerable to physical attacks.

sections.heading: Phase 1: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.markdown:
Rennala's first phase occurs in a circular room with an open inner area and a more narrow outer area, divided by bookcases. Rennala floats around the room encased in a golden sphere that prevents her from taking damage. The majority of her Juvenile Scholars congregate in the inner arena, however a few can be found hiding behind the bookcases.

Rennala rarely attacks directly during this phase. Instead, the Juvenile Scholars lunge, breathe fire, and use telekinesis to assault the player with the books and globes. They also drop chandeliers from the ceiling if the player stands underneath them. However, Rennala periodically converts scholars to gravestones, which she sends flying towards the player. She also summons new Scholars to replace those the player has slain.

One of the Scholars sings, surrounded by a golden aura. The song grows louder as the player draws near. Hitting the singing Scholar at least once—without necessarily killing them—causes another to begin singing. Disrupt three singing Scholars to shatter Rennala’s sphere, dropping her to the ground and leaving her vulnerable. While she lies stunned, the Scholars cease their attacks, giving the player an opening to strike. After a few seconds, Rennala releases a golden explosion and rises again, her protective sphere restored. Repeating this process several times creates additional opportunities to damage her.

Defeating Rennala triggers a cutscene, and advances the fight to Phase Two. A spell placed by Ranni the Witch on the amber egg activates, releasing a dense fog of darkness.

sections.heading: Phase 2: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
sections.markdown:
After the cutscene, the arena transforms into a vast, moonlit watery plane with no obstacles or clutter. Ranni's illusory Rennala engages the player directly with a full health bar. She relies primarily on ranged magical attacks but also swings her staff to strike if the player approaches too closely.

When her health drops below 60%, she begins summoning spirits for assistance. Each time she summons, a glowing circle expands around her, dealing damage to anything within it. She can call forth a Bloodhound Knight, three wolves, a Flying Dragon, or a Troll Knight, each lasting only a few seconds before vanishing. During this phase, Rennala moves more evasively, making it difficult for melee fighters to land consistent attack chains.

Moving away from Rennala's homing attacks is simple, as there is nothing to get stuck on or blocked in by. However, there is nothing to separate Rennala from her summoned allies.

sections.heading: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon (NPC)
sections.markdown:
After defeating her, Rennala becomes an NPC, remaining in the library where she was fought in phase 1. As an NPC she offers two services: **Rebirth** allows the player to reallocate levels to different stats at the cost of a Larval Tear, while **Cosmetics** allows the player to alter their character's appearance, which is the same function that the mirror in Roundtable Hold has.

When Sorceress Sellen moves to the Academy of Raya Lucaria during her questline, she will temporarily occupy Rennala's spot, while Rennala will move behind one of the bookshelves in the library. She will return to her usual place once Sellen's questline is completed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Wears the Queen's Set and wields the Carian Regal Scepter as her Glintstone staff. It is one of the best staffs in the game and it enhances full moon sorceries.
- Rennala survives their fight and may interact with the player. She is always found in the Grand Library at the top of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
- After Rennala is defeated, she allows players to change their appearance or reallocate their stats using her Rebirth magic. The process requires Larval Tears.
- When Sellen takes over the Academy, Rennala can still be found in the Grand Library, hiding behind some bookshelves. When Sellen eventually turns into a Graven Mass, Rennala is back in her place while Sellen is moved to the side of the library where she remains for the rest of the game.
- The approach to the Grand Library which houses Rennala is guarded by Moongrum, one of the last Carian Knights who once served the Lunar Queen. A Mad Pumpkin Head and Giant Silver Tear also protect the route.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ranni the Witch**, also known as **Lunar Princess Ranni** and **Renna the Witch**, is a character in Elden Ring. She is one of the Demigods, and the focus of one of the game's most elaborate questlines.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
A child born of the union between Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon and red-haired Radagon during the age of the Erdtree, Ranni embodied an alliance between Raya Lucaria and Leyndell. She had two older brothers, Radahn and Rykard. As a daughter of the Carian Queen, she was a Lunar Princess, and first heir in the royal line. Led by the hand of her mother, young Ranni encountered her Dark Moon—cold, dark, and veiled in occult mystery.

The Two Fingers named Ranni as an Empyrean, one with the potential to one day succeed Queen Marika as the divine ruler of the Lands Between, and granted her a Shadowbound Beast named Blaidd to be her vassal. He was approved of by Rennala and was raised as her foster brother. Ranni grew up playing with Blaidd, and they were often accompanied by Iji, a troll blacksmith who served the Carian royals.

At some point, Ranni's father abandoned her mother to marry Queen Marika and assume the title of second Elden Lord. Although Ranni and her siblings were raised to Demigod status by their new stepmother, their heartbroken mother was left indisposed, cradling her Amber Egg in all-consuming grief.

Ranni later ventured deep in woods, where she encountered a snowy crone who became her secret mentor. She was an old witch well versed in cold-based sorceries, and she taught Ranni to fear the Dark Moon as she imparted her magic. The full Dark Moon, cold and leaden, would become Ranni's sigil and symbol of her power and authority.

sections.heading: The Night of Black Knives
sections.markdown:
Although the Two Fingers had chosen her as Marika's successor, Ranni did not wish to be a puppet for the Greater Will and resented her Empyrean fate. In order to escape it, Ranni stole a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh, the Black Blade and, through a fearsome rite, imbued it into the blades of Numen assassins, who were said to be close to Queen Marika herself. She also gave a fragment to her brother Rykard as a last resort, so he could kill Maliketh if necessary. Ranni plotted for the assassins to kill another individual while she simultaneously killed herself, slaying her own body while the other person died in spirit, thus freeing herself from being an Empyrean.

In what would become known as the Night of Black Knives, the assassins murdered Godwyn the Golden, killing him in spirit, while Ranni killed herself in body, transferring her spirit into a doll said to be modeled after the image of her mentor, the Snow Witch. This marked the step-siblings as the first demigod casualties in history. Ranni's fate and her involvement in the plot remained largely unknown by the denizens of the Lands Between.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.markdown: At some point after the Night of Black Knives, Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring. Ranni claimed a Great Rune, but appears to have discarded it, and largely remained outside of the conflict that followed. As a consequence of her doll body, Ranni required extended periods of hibernation and withdrew from the world, hiding in the Carian Manor while her agents worked to bring about her plan of ridding the Lands Between of the influence of the Greater Will, allowing her to pursue her divine ascension on her own terms.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown:
After the Shattering, Ranni learned of a recently arrived Tarnished riding the spectral steed, Torrent. She approached them at the Church of Elleh, inquiring whether they possess the steed that once accompanied Melina. Upon confirming her suspicions, she bestowed upon them a Spirit Calling Bell and Lone Wolf Ashes, explaining that Torrent’s former master had entrusted her with delivering these items to its next owner.

Ranni later reunited with the Tarnished at her Rise in the Three Sisters, where she invited them into her service. She tasked the Tarnished with aiding Blaidd in uncovering a path into Nokron, Eternal City, to claim its treasure—a weapon capable of slaying the Two Fingers who had chosen her as an Empyrean. However, the path to Nokron would only reveal itself with the death of her brother, Starscourge Radahn, who had long held the stars—and thus Ranni's fate—in stasis with gravity magic.

After Radahn's defeat and the acquisition of the Fingerslayer Blade, Ranni descended to the Ainsel River Main, leading to Nokstella, Eternal City. There, she commanded her champion to rid her of the Baleful Shadows sent by the Two Fingers to assassinate her. Upon their victory, Ranni rewarded the Tarnished with a key to a Carian chest containing the Dark Moon Ring. Then, Ranni departed to fulfill her dark purpose. She traveled to the Cathedral of Manus Celes on the Moonlight Altar, where she slew the great Two Fingers beneath it and abandoned her doll body.

If the Tarnished retrieved the Dark Moon Ring and presented it to Ranni's doll, she accepted them as her consort, granting them the Dark Moon Greatsword as a symbol of their union. She revealed the full extent of her plan: to succeed Queen Marika as god and bring about the Age of the Stars. Ranni intends to remove the Elden Ring from the Lands Between and journey into the cosmos, freeing its inhabitants from the influence of the Greater Will and granting them true autonomy over their lives.

After defeating the Elden Beast, the Tarnished may summon Ranni, who ushers in the Dark Moon and her Age of the Stars, realizing her vision for a new Order.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: Ranni's disembodied spirit inhabits the woven puppet of a four-armed maiden with pallid blue skin and long, flowing blue hair. Her left eye—the doll's right—is sealed shut by an azure sigil, while both open eyes glow cyan. She wears an elegant white gown beneath a voluminous fur cloak, lined with two long brown braids. A massive, floppy-brimmed witch’s hat rests atop her head, crowned with a delicate silver filigree. Luminious blue veinwork runs throughout the frozen brim's cold underside.

sections.heading: Ranni's Quest
sections.markdown:
- Completing Ranni's quest will result in the "Age of the Stars" ending.
- Her questline intersects with the following NPCs: Blaidd the Half-Wolf, Castellan Jerren, Fia, Deathbed Companion, Pidia, Carian Servant, Preceptor Seluvis, Smithing Master Iji, and Sorcerer Rogier.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.markdown:
1. *(Optional)* Church of Elleh
 - After meeting Melina and obtaining the Spectral Steed Whistle, use Torrent at least once. After that, rest on any Site of Grace. Then, fast travel to the Church of Elleh Site of Grace and find Ranni (using the pseudonym "**Renna the Witch**") sitting on a broken wall. Exhaust her dialogue to receive the Spirit Calling Bell and Lone Wolf Ashes for free.
 - If you miss this step, these items will be available for purchase at the Twin Maiden Husks in Roundtable Hold— 200 runes for the Lone Wolf Ashes and 1,000 runes for the Spirit Calling Bell respectively.
1. Caria Manor
 - Traverse Caria Manor in northwestern Liurnia of the Lakes.
 - Defeat the apparition of Royal Knight Loretta at the Royal Moongazing Grounds, which unlocks the path to Three Sisters behind her.
1. Ranni's Rise
 - Ranni can next be encountered on the top floor of her Rise in the Three Sisters. This stage varies depending on whether you have met her before, defeated Starscourge Radahn, or given Sorcerer Rogier the Black Knifeprint.
 - Agree to become one of Ranni's vassals, and then head back down the tower to speak to the projections of Iji, Blaidd, and Seluvis. After speaking to all three, return to Ranni and speak to her again. After this point, if you return to Ranni, she will be sleeping and non-responsive.
 - *(Optional)* Administer Preceptor Seluvis's Amber Draught to Ranni. She will awaken. Speak to her three times, and she will banish you from her sight.
 - **WARNING:** This will permanently end Preceptor Seluvis and Pidia, Carian Servant's quests.
 - **WARNING:** Ranni's questline will no longer progress; however, this can be undone by using Celestial Dew to receive absolution at the Church of Vows.
1. Caelid
 - Defeat Starscourge Radahn to resume the movement of the stars.
1. Nokron, Eternal City
 - Nokron can only be accessed via the *Starfall Crater* in east Limgrave after defeating Starscourge Radahn.
 - Proceed through the area to obtain the Fingerslayer Blade, which is in a chest northeast of the Night's Sacred Ground Site of Grace.
1. Three Sisters
 - Travel to Ranni's Rise and deliver the Fingerslayer Blade to Ranni, who will give you the Carian Inverted Statue.
 - This key item is required to progress Fia, Deathbed Companion's questline. However, it is *not* necessary to complete Ranni's quest.
 - **WARNING:** This will permanently end Preceptor Seluvis and Pidia, Carian Servant's quest.
 - Travel to Renna's Rise, which unseals after Ranni departs with the Fingerslayer Blade. Enter and climb to the top, and go through the Sending Gate to the upper portion of Ainsel River.
1. Ainsel River Main
 - Pick up the Miniature Ranni near the spawn point and rest at the Ainsel River Main Site of Grace. Use the "Talk to miniature Ranni" option three times to get her to speak.
1. Nokstella, Eternal City
 - *(Optional)* Ranni will also have dialogue at the Nokstella, Eternal City and Nokstella Waterfall Basin Sites of Grace. These are not required to continue her questline.
 - Defeat the Baleful Shadow invader just past the Nokstella Waterfall Basin Site of Grace to obtain the Discarded Palace Key.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria
 - Defeat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon at the Raya Lucaria Grand Library.
 - Unlock the chest behind Rennala and obtain the Dark Moon Ring.
1. Lake of Rot
 - Ride the Transportation Coffin at the Grand Cloister. Defeat Astel, Naturalborn of the Void and then travel up the lift. However, this lift remains locked until the player obtains the Dark Moon Ring.
1. Moonlight Altar
 - Travel to the Cathedral of Manus Celes and descend through the tunnel near the altar to find Ranni sitting on the corpse of her Two Fingers. Interact with her to trigger a cutscene. After the cutscene, speak to her again, and she will disappear, bequeathing the Dark Moon Greatsword.
1. Stone Platform
 - After defeating the final boss, there will be a blue summon sign beside Fractured Marika. Interact with it to summon Ranni, allowing you to achieve the Age of the Stars ending.
 - **WARNING:** Ranni's summon sign will not appear if the player has met with the Three Fingers. This can be undone by defeating both Malenia, Goddess of Rot and Dragonlord Placidusax, and using Miquella's Needle in the latter's boss arena at Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Wears the Snow Witch Set: Snow Witch Hat, Snow Witch Robe, Snow Witch Skirt

- Ranni cannot be killed but will vanish if attacked. She will reappear if the player uses Celestial Dew to receive absolution at the Church of Vows.

- Ranni inhabits a doll body resembling the Snow Witch, her former master. She later inhabits miniature versions of it. It is unclear whether it was made by the Nox of the Eternal Cities, Ranni, or the snow witch herself.

- Ranni's original Empyrean body can be found atop the Divine Tower of Liurnia and still possesses one-half of the Cursemark of Death.
 - Examining the blackened remains closely reveals hints of red hair on her head, which is characteristic of a daughter of Radagon.
 - Ranni's original body has two arms, while her doll body has four. It is thus similar to Miquella the Kind and the Marionette soldiers utilized by Sorcerers throughout the game.
 - The Stargazer Heirloom can be found on her body as well, a memento of her mother Rennala.

- Certain stages of Ranni's questline trigger Seluvis to go inert and Pidia to die at the hands of puppets of Raya Lucaria Soldiers. This outcome occurs either if Ranni is offered the Amber Draught or after she receives the Fingerslayer Blade and departs from Caria Manor.
 - The Cuckoo soldiers participated in the Siege of Caria Manor but were defeated by the Carian's magic.

- If the player administers the Amber Draught to Ranni, she will awaken and express her disappointment in them for indulging Seluvis before banishing them from her sight. Should the player persist in attempting to speak with her, Ranni will instantly kill them. This transgression may also be forgiven through absolution at the Church of Vows.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Ranni's body was imbued with frost magic, releasing a cold so intense that even Blaidd, that covered his armor with a pelt, was still bothered.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Radagon of the Golden Order** is a boss in Elden Ring. He is encountered inside the Erdtree in Leyndell, Ashen Capital, and is the first half of the final boss fight, with the Elden Beast as the second half.

sections.heading: Liurnian Wars and Marriage to Queen Rennala
sections.markdown:
Radagon first rose to prominence during the Liurnian Wars, when he joined the heroes' ranks. A great champion with flowing red locks, he arrived in Liurnia at the head of a golden host, where he met Queen Rennala in battle. Although two wars would be fought between them, the First and Second Liurnian Wars,, no victor would emerge from either. Radagon eventually repented his territorial aggressions by cleansing himself with Celestial Dew, and swore his love to Rennala. He became husband to the Carian Queen, wedding her at the Church of Vows. Rennala bequeathed him a greatsword, bestowed by a Carian queen upon her spouse to honor long-standing tradition. After entering into marriage with Rennala and joining the Carian line, he ordered the Carian magic preceptors to don masks of confidence, to make it clear that all of their matters were to be kept strictly private.

Radagon and Rennala had three children: Radahn, Rykard and Ranni. While husband to Rennala, Radagon studied glintstone sorcery taught at the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

After Godfrey, the First Elden Lord was stripped of grace and hounded from the Lands Between, Radagon returned to the capital where he went on to marry Queen Marika and become her King Consort and second Elden Lord. Before leaving Rennala, Radagon gifted her an amber egg. His departure left her heartbroken, and eventually led to her being deposed by the academy and imprisoned in the Grand Library. His three children from the previous marriage would be raised to demigod status as stepchildren of Queen Marika.

sections.heading: Marriage to Queen Marika
sections.markdown:
A sculptor from Leyndell was commissioned to create a statue of Radagon. In doing so, he discovered a secret - that Radagon is Marika. This secret was hidden within the statue, and is revealed by casting Law of Regression in front of it, causing the statue's form to change from Radagon to Marika.

Radagon and Marika had a twin daughter and son: Malenia and Miquella. As they were born of a single god, they were both Empyreans, but were born afflicted: Malenia with a rotting sickness and Miquella with eternal childhood.

While married to Marika, Radagon studied incantations. He is heavily associated with Golden Order Fundamentalism, a branch of the Golden Order said to be scholarship in all but name, which incorporates incantations that rely on a combination of faith and intelligence. His son Miquella followed in his fundamentalist footsteps, and created several incantations as gifts for his father. Radagon would return the favor with his own gift of gratitude to young Miquella, however Miquella later abandoned Fundamentalism, realising that it could do nothing to treat Malenia's Rot.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.markdown:
Following the Night of Black Knives, Marika shattered the Elden Ring, breaking the Golden Order. Radagon, on the other hand, remained loyal to the Golden Order, and attempted to repair the Elden Ring with the same hammer used to shatter it. As punishment, Marika was imprisoned inside the Erdtree. While Radagon had opposed Marika's treachery, he would share Marika's sentence, as the two were now bound in a single body.

When a Tarnished sets fire to the Erdtree in order to burn away the wall of thorns denying their entry, they encounter the imprisoned Marika. Suddenly released from her bonds, her hair immediately turns red as Radagon assumes control of their shared body and wields Marika's hammer to fight the Tarnished. However, Radagon is unable to defeat them and falls at their hands, with his body being subsumed by the Elden Beast to transform into a large sword, as it emerges to be the Tarnished champion's final challenge.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.markdown: Radagon is the first of two enemies that compose the final boss fight of Elden Ring, with the Elden Beast being the second. Players will have to fight Radagon again if they die to the Elden Beast.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.markdown:
Radagon relies on very fast hammer swings, and some of his attacks will generate shockwaves. These shockwaves will either be immediate, or will occur after a brief delay- for the latter, golden cracks will appear in the ground moments before the explosion.

At range, Radagon can throw golden spears at the player. He will either leap into the air and throw a single, giant spear, or quickly hurl five spears in a loose fan. These spears will remain in the ground for a second before exploding. He also has a grab attack which he may perform at close- or mid-range. During the grab, his left arm will glow gold and he will wind it back behind him before lunging. The shockwave generated by the grab may still cause damage even if the grab itself misses.

All of his gold attacks will inflict Holy damage.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.markdown: After his health has been lowered somewhat, he will leap into the air and perform a Gold Breaker attack, creating a large area of effect shockwave. During this phase, Radagon will sometimes teleport, generating an explosion when he reappears. In addition to the golden spear attacks used in the previous phase, he may now jump up and throw a volley of spears. His stomp will also now create a shockwave that deals Holy damage.

sections.heading: Phase 3
sections.markdown: Once his health is below half, Radagon will teleport into the middle of the arena and perform three rapid hammer strikes on the ground, each producing a large shockwave. He will now teleport much more often, and can perform two shockwave-inducing hammer strikes in quick succession.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.markdown: The arena is a featureless, oval platform with no obstacles. It is not possible to fall of the edges.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown: - This boss can be cheesed by running up to him as soon as possible and blocking his way. The AI doesn't become aggressive until it has made a certain number of steps, so you can take him down with ease as long as you have a way to deal damage without moving (bows, damage dealing auras, etc). This can also be done by running up to him as soon as possible, performing a jump attack (so landing too low for his line of sight), and quickly sidestepping behind him. You are then most likely free to make multiple strong attacks on him until his guard is broken, perform a critical hit, charge a strong attack again while he's standing up, and start the fight proper at that point onward with roughly half his health already gone.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Radagon needs to be parried multiple times to trigger a stagger.
- Radagon was said to have despised his own red hair, as it was perhaps the result of a curse by red-haired Fire Giants. Ironically, most of his children would inherit it, and some of them would even be proud of its heroic implications.
- Radagon's rune can be seen in Radagon's Scarseal, Radagon's Soreseal, and in the thorns blocking the Erdtree. It resembles the criss-cross pattern seen in his statues, and is reminiscent of a sewing pattern, as he was also associated with sewing needles, perhaps symbolizing his need to keep things held together.
- The Radagon Icon mentions how he studied sorcery as husband of Rennala, and incantations as husband of Marika, aspiring to be complete.
- When Marika's body changes into Radagon, her dress becomes his skirt.
 - Queen Marika and Lord Radagon wear the same black outfit with gold floral patterns in their side profile paintings at the Roundtable Hold, teasing their secret at an early point in the game's narrative.
- The Revenant's ghost stares at a Radagon painting at the Roundtable Hold in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Internal name: **MaricaOfDistorted** (ID: 2190)
- Radagon/Marika are reminiscent of the alchemical Red King and White Queen, who are often depicted as the two halves of the Rebis. In alchemy, the Rebis is a single being possessing both male and female qualities, also sometimes referred to as the divine hermaphrodite. It is said that the Rebis originated from a being that was divided into male and female halves, until it was unified again to form a transcendental being empowered by a dragon.
- Lord Radagon prophesied the Tarnisheds' return in .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Putrescence** (泥濘, *Deinei*, lit. Muddy mud) is a material in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Congealed Putrescence was a bruise-colored ooze that formed from the tainted, impure remains of heroes housed within the stone coffin ships. Decorated with sculptures of bulls, beasts, and the bearded god of the Ancient Dynasty, they were sent off with Great Grave Glovewort for burial at sea. The colossal arks drifted to the Southern Shore of the Gravesite Plain since time immemorial, washing up on its Cerulean Coast.

Although the tainted flesh had putrified into a foul liquor by the time they washed ashore on the Lands Between's Cerulean Coast, it nonetheless received the cleansing Death rites of the time: incineration by cold ghostflame in the kilns of the Deathbirds. At some point, the ghostflame practices ended, and the coffins accumulated over time in the Stone Coffin Fissure, where their leaked contents formed stalactites and dripped down into the chasm.

After Shattering, Miquella the Kind embarked on a pilgrimage through the Realm of Shadow. When he visited the Stone Coffin Fissure, he abandoned his love and other self, casting St. Trina down into the depths. Though wounded, Trina survived, and soon her presence transformed the area into the Garden of Deep Purple. When the sludge imbibed her velvety nectar, it received its long sought-after eternal rest, and coalesced into her Putrescent Knight.

The original sin was the first and gravest of the many blasphemous crimes committed by Queen Marika and her Erdtree, though its exact nature remains shrouded in mystery. Its evidence was sealed away in the Realm of Shadow by Marika when Messmer the Impaler launched the crusade.

Miquella the Kind sought to erase the original sin by abandoning everything and ascending to godhood at the Gate of Divinity. He discarded parts of his being along his pilgrimage through the Shadow Realm, a Miquella's Cross forming at each stop.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Regal Ancestor Spirit** is an optional Remembrance boss in Elden Ring. It is encountered at the northern Hallowhorn Grounds along the Siofra River after lighting six bonfires.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Deer-like spirits found in Siofra River. They exist beyond the purview of the Erdtree, and follow the principle that life sprouts from death as it does from birth. This process is reflected by their horns, which sprout new growths even after the ancestor's death. Shamans of the Ancestral Followers don headdresses fashioned from horns with buds, mirroring the appearance of the ancestor spirits.

Ancestor Spirits appear emaciated, with exposed ribs, matted fur, and cavities in their chests. They have large, antler-like horns which glow and sprout small buds.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: An Ancestor Spirit is found in the upper part of Siofra River at the northern Hallowhorn Grounds, north-east of Night's Sacred Ground and the Ancestral Woods Site of Grace. Much like the other Ancestor Spirit, this one can only be fought after lighting flames- in this case six- in the surrounding area and then touching the horned remains.

sections.heading: Boss fight
sections.markdown: Although it initially fights in much the same way as the standard Ancestor Spirit, once its health has been reduce to half it will start to heal itself by siphoning HP from the player, as well as from the spirit animals in the arena. It will also sometimes collapse and fade away, and then emerge from one of the other animals in the arena. It can also use abilities reminiscent of other animals- hopping like a springhare, charging like a boar, or curling into a ball and rolling like a goat.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - In Norse mythology, eat among the branches of the world tree . According to the , the stags crane their necks upward to chomp at the branches. The morning dew gathers in their horns and forms the rivers of the world.

Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 7,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Golden Order Principia.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
 - WARNING: Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Creates a halo of light above the caster's head, which is then thrown out as an expanding ring of light around them, with Holy Attack Power equal to 310% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 395% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 37 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 48 points of Stamina.
- Deals 10 Stance damage on a hit, increasing to 14 Stance damage if charged.
- Attack Power is boosted by 10% per Golden Order Seal held in an active hand (2 max) and by 15% per Dryleaf Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
 - Since it's possible to acquire both of these Seals in one Playthrough, it's one of a few spells able to stack Seal boosts (for a total boost of 27% in this case).
- Wearing the Radiant Gold Mask increases Attack Power by 10%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
 - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 27%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 46%.
- While its large hitbox would seem able to hit large targets multiple times, it can actually only hit a target once.
 - This makes it less able to hit weak spots on large foes, since the large hitbox can fairly easily hit another, non-weak body part beforehand.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Actually consists of 16 separate but overlapping projectiles.
- Patch 1.07 reduced FP consumption and recovery time.
 - FP cost was reduced from 25 to 21.
- Patch 1.04 decreased FP cost, increased damage, and cast speed. Decreased recovery time.
 - FP cost was reduced from 29 to 25.
 - Attack Power was increased from 282% of Incantation Scaling to 310% of the same for the uncharged version and from 333% of Incantation Scaling to 395% of the same for the charged version.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: Chelona's Rise, in the south-west of the Moonfolk Ruins. You'll have to solve the puzzle with the three spirit turtles. One is right next to the Rise, the other at the cliff south-east of the Lunar Estate Ruins on a ledge and the third is flying above the evergaol portal in the north-west. You'll have to start at Chelona's Rise and travel to each location by foot/horse, otherwise the turtles don't spawn.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Trade the Remembrance of the Full Moon Queen, gained by defeating Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, with Finger Reader Enia.

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums with a bell to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Rock Blaster** is a spell in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Loot:** Caelid
- Acquired from a corpse in a shed at the upper levels of Sellia Crystal Tunnel.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
POWER (shockwave): 291% SS.

POWER (held movement): 36% SS per tick 5 FP each, roughly 5 ticks per second.

A very short-ranged shockwave that is a bit slow to fire, and is fairly inefficient in FP cost. You will be quite vulnerable to counterattacks during this and will exhaust your FP quickly.
